precision_scope.evaluation: binary64, worse of the fused and separate multiply-add routes
precision_scope.count_unit: coefficients of one representation of the fit
precision_scope.why_fp64: the count trade is resolved at the double lane's 1e-13 F_0 contract; the nearest-neighbour comparison is 5e-14 absolute in binary64; and a binary64 coefficient is 8 bytes while a binary32 one is 4, so counts from the two lanes are not like-for-like storage
precision_scope.fp32_in_this_paper: static counts only, a secondary column; not part of the width law
precision_scope.sweep_scope: fp64 only: binary64 stored coefficients, binary64 evaluation, targets rel:1e-13 and abs:5e-14
precision_scope.fp32_comparison_would_need: the float lane's own path: fits stored and evaluated in binary32, both multiply-add routes, certified at max(2^-22 F_n(x), 1.5e-7) from the generator's f32 fit and acceptance functions, on the float lane's own edges and partitions

meta.matched_ratio: every width is the Group A width multiplied by 2, so W/a is the Group A W/x0
meta.reference: 1/sqrt(x) at 60-digit working precision (mpmath.sqrt, 20 digits above the working precision); the generator's boys_ref is replaced by this exact value and its cheb_coeffs builds the interpolant from it. The rational solvers are the generator's, unchanged.
meta.target_note: rel targets are relative to f; abs:5e-14 is an absolute error on f, unscaled (the paper's absolute arm is F_0(a)-scaled through L; the analysis states the model convention it uses)
